sources.title: László Tapolcai: Can the tribal character of the early Piast centre be established?
sources.note: 2017 article abstract: Polanie first attested around 1000; author argues that the name denoted subjects of Bolesław rather than a securely established earlier tribe. Argument attributed, not represented as unanimous consensus.

sources.title: National Institute of Cultural Heritage: Bonikowo hillfort
sources.note: Elżbieta Wyrwińska, 2014. History and excavation sections: open village sixth to eighth centuries, fort first half ninth century, timbers after 815/826; later houses and mixed find assemblage explicitly separated. Introductory tribal attribution not adopted as certain.

sources.title: Elżbieta Indycka: Giecz cemetery and settlement excavations, 1999 and 2000
sources.note: Archaeological reserve primary excavation report. Direct fetch failed; full indexed original returned by query site.giecz.pl VIII 1999-2000 osadnictwa. Summary assigns early settlement eighth/ninth, later settlement tenth/first half eleventh and cemetery second half eleventh/twelfth. Wooden road belongs to later settlement, stylus to cemetery.

sources.title: Joanna Koszałka: Between stronghold and village, plant economy of early medieval Poznań
sources.note: 2008, printed pages 127 to 137. Later Piast-period comparison, not eighth-century evidence. Pages 129 to 131 cereal/weed deposits and braided storage pits; pages 131 to 132 processing utensil and probable ovens.

sources.title: National Museum in Kraków: Bolesław denar MNK VII-P-769
sources.note: Exact PRINCES POLONIE and translation władca Polski in Mateusz Woźniak object commentary. Heading dates 1000 to 1010, Gniezno uncertain; bird interpreted as peacock. Full indexed original checked with query site.zbiory.mnk.pl/pl/katalog/525741 PRINCES POLONIE. Erroneous diameter metadata omitted.

sources.title: Oleksiy Tolochko: Poliany, Encyclopedia of the History of Ukraine
sources.note: 2013 entry, revised 2021. Full indexed original at resource.history.org.ua and holodomor-era.history.org.ua CGI mirrors. Origin-story genre, name no longer current in chronicler’s day, absent from Constantine VII and no unambiguous material identification. Same article counted once across mirrors.

sources.title: George Yurii Shevelov: Rus’, Internet Encyclopedia of Ukraine
sources.note: First paragraph only: conventional Polianian land around Kyiv between Dnipro, Irpin and Ros. Does not substantiate imported northern reach to 62 N. Other broader etymological assertions not adopted.

sources.title: Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies: Kyi
sources.note: Semi-legendary figure and Primary Chronicle story of three brothers and sister. Explicitly a story, not evidence for a precise founding date.

sources.title: Johan Callmer: Urbanisation in Northern and Eastern Europe, circa 700 to 1100
sources.note: Printed page 257: ninth-century plateau settlements, late-ninth growth, early Podil and buildings. Direct PDF failed; full indexed original returned by query Callmer Urbanisation Kiev 257. No disputed exact church date or population estimate adopted.

sources.title: Johan Callmer: The Archaeology of Kiev to the End of the Earliest Urban Phase
sources.note: Harvard Ukrainian Studies 11 (1987), pages 323 to 364, especially 337. Full indexed journal PDF checked via patriotyk.name mirror; query ARCHAEOLOGY OF KIEV 337 300. Three passages under 200 combined words from same article. No exact 887 certainty.

sources.title: Thomas S. Noonan: The emergence of Kiev as a commercial and industrial centre
sources.note: Archaeological News 5 (1998), author’s extended English abstract hosted by Institute for History of Material Culture. Indexed original full text checked; direct fetch failed. Growth section distinguishes most of tenth century from circa 1000 glass/amber expansion; workshop count is sample, not census.

sources.title: Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies: Church of the Tithes
sources.note: Construction 989 to 996 and princely tithe; surviving fragments. One passage only; public contemporary context distinct from tribal attribution.

sources.title: National Museum of the History of Ukraine: floor mosaics of the Church of the Tithes
sources.note: Museum distinguishes Leonid Totsky modern reconstruction from original fragments held at Sophia Kyivska. Fragments found 1824, geometric/checkerboard coloured marble/slate/glass design.

sources.title: Susana Torres Prieto and Benjamin Outhwaite: A reassessment of the Kyivan letter from the Cairo Genizah
sources.note: Direct full 15-page scholarly text checked at api.repository.cam.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/59160656-ec74-446b-b681-6d685d71d87a/content. Landing URL matches runtime Khazars source for cumulative budget. PDF page 3 edition line 6 קהילות קדושות, no reconstructed letters in this excerpt; translation PDF page 5 line 6. Dating discussion PDF pages 2, 7, 9 and final page: tenth/eleventh, preferred late tenth or eleventh. Do not claim precise 930 or certain Khazar authorship. Translation lines 8 to 17 supplies debt story, 60 paid and 40 still owed.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Decoded geometry lies in western/central Poland, 700 to 800, bbox 15.93196 to 21.91882 E, 50.71554 to 53.17496 N. Distinct from Kyiv Polyanians. Neither boundary nor eighth-century polity is authenticated. Sparse contemporary evidence handled openly; later Bonikowo fort, Giecz road/stylus and Poznań food/coin examples explicitly labelled later. No exact midpoint years.

Decoded imported footprint 900 to 1000, bbox 26.57007 to 35.34695 E, 48.57962 to 62.07948 N: gross northern excess far beyond conventional Kyiv/Dnipro/Irpin/Ros area. Public overview warns directly. Distinct from western Polanes. Related Kyiv/Rus runtime cards do not establish direct identity; no alias. Hebrew letter broader tenth/eleventh date and religious community explicitly distinguished from tribal vernacular.
